1.name: comment

2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
smpl_mag_yaw_correct turns joints of an SMPL pose about the vertical, to undo heading errors that come from the suit's magnetometers.

WHAT IT TAKES:
An SMPL pose in AXIS-ANGLE form, at least 22 joints. Joints past the 22nd pass through untouched. A pose in quaternions produces no output at all - from shadow_to_smpl, set 'output_format' to axis_angle.

Set 'up axis' to match the pose. It defaults to Y, but shadow_to_smpl sends Z-up by default, and a heading correction about the wrong axis is a tilt.

EACH JOINT IS CORRECTED WHERE IT IS IN THE ROOM:
The node works out every joint's orientation in the room, turns each one, and then works the pose back out from the corrected orientations. So a correction on the upper arm turns the upper arm alone: the forearm stays where it was in the room. That matches the problem, because each sensor has its own heading error.

TWO CORRECTIONS PER JOINT:
Each joint has two values, in degrees.

The first, named after the joint (left_shoulder), turns the joint about the room's vertical. This is the one for heading drift: the whole sensor reading rotated in the room.

The second, named with _cal (left_shoulder_cal), turns it about the vertical axis in the joint's own frame - so its effect follows the joint as it moves.

'sync local/global' keeps the two equal. Equal values leave a joint that is in the rest orientation - or turned from it only about the vertical - exactly as it is; the correction shows as the joint tilts away. That is right when a sensor's heading error is the same whichever way it faces, and not otherwise, so it is a convenience rather than a setting to leave on regardless.

After the conversion from the suit to SMPL the _cal value is no longer the sensor's own calibration offset; treat it as a heading adjustment that travels with the joint.

SYNTAX:
smpl_mag_yaw_correct

EXAMPLE:
smpl_mag_yaw_correct

INPUTS and PROPERTIES:

pose in:
The axis-angle pose.

up axis:
Y or Z: which way is up in the pose.

symmetric:
Editing a left joint copies the same value to the right one, and the other way round.

sync local/global:
Editing either value of a joint copies it to the other.

Both act when you edit a value; ticking them does not change values already set.

reset:
Set every value back to zero.

pelvis ... right_wrist, pelvis_cal ... right_wrist_cal:
The two corrections for each joint, in degrees.

OUTPUT:

pose out:
The corrected pose, one row per joint.

RELATED:
mag_yaw_correct does the same correction on the suit side, per sensor, before the pose becomes SMPL at all. Correcting there is better when you can, because it fixes the measurement rather than its consequences. smpl_pose_adjust adds a fixed rotation to any joint, in the joint's frame or its parent's.
